title: Calendar arithmetic
description:
`timedelta` has no months or years, so write the calendar helpers yourself (with `datetime.date`):

```python
def add_months(d, n): ...              # same day n months later (or earlier); clamp to the month's last day
def age_on(birthday, day): ...          # whole years old on `day`
def workdays_between(start, end): ...   # Monday-Friday dates d with start <= d < end
def next_weekday(d, weekday): ...       # the first date AFTER d with that weekday (0 = Monday)
```

`add_months(date(2026, 1, 31), 1)` is `date(2026, 2, 28)`; `add_months(date(2024, 3, 31), -1)` is `date(2024, 2, 29)`. Someone born on 29 February is a year older on 1 March in non-leap years (they have not had a 29 February yet on 28 February). `workdays_between` returns 0 when `end <= start`.
hints: Count months from year 0 (`year * 12 + month - 1`), add `n`, and split back with `divmod(total, 12)`; then clamp the day with `calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]`, the number of days in that month.
For the age, comparing `(month, day)` tuples tells whether the birthday has happened yet this year.
